comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C79-C84 regarding the novel state-dependent outer leaflet intersubunit lipid site. Both evaluations find this supported, with peer reviewers explicitly highlighting it as a strength and noting its relevance to modulation sites in other pLGICs.

Strong agreement on claims C48-C56 regarding inner-leaflet lipid sites. Both evaluations support these findings, with peer reviewers acknowledging the novelty of the complementary site and accepting the state-independence demonstrated by superimposable densities.

Strong agreement on claims C23, C24, C36, C89 regarding the cryo-EM structure quality and lipid density identification. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes a caveat about lipid identity determination (C102-C103), while peer reviewers emphasize the convincing nature of the structural data and agreement with simulations. Peer review also includes C38 regarding forked density shapes.

Agreement on claims C57-C61, C113 regarding saturation-dependent lipid binding modes. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight the W217 mutational analysis (C62-C64, C112) as supporting evidence, connecting it to conserved residues and neurosteroid binding sites in other pLGICs.

Both address mutational analysis claims C62-C64, C112. OpenEval supports the findings but notes limited statistical power (8 vs 100 trajectories). Peer reviewers strongly support the W217 findings, emphasizing functional relevance across pLGICs without raising statistical concerns.

Both address state-dependent outer leaflet sites (C71-C75, C116). OpenEval supports findings but notes modest quantitative differences and need for experimental validation. Peer reviewers accept the state-dependent differences and note simulations provide solid basis for predictions. Peer review also covers C26-C27, C65-C68, C115.

Partial overlap on outer-leaflet sites C65-C68. OpenEval supports pH-insensitivity findings (C69-C70) but suggests qualification regarding conformational state vs pH effects. Peer reviewers accept outer leaflet findings as part of broader state-dependent analysis without challenging pH interpretation.

Both address lipid dynamics and exchange (C43-C47). OpenEval supports diffusion coefficient calculations and exchange event conclusions. Peer reviewers explicitly validate the simulation timescales based on diffusion analysis, though note longer simulations would be needed for interaction strength determination.

Both address structural-simulation correspondence (C39-C42). OpenEval supports the integration and quantitative analysis. Peer reviewers affirm the general agreement between structures and simulations increases confidence in lipid interaction poses.

Both address simulation sampling adequacy (C96-C100). OpenEval supports the diffusion analysis as evidence of adequate sampling while acknowledging 1.7 µs may limit very stable interactions. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the diffusion coefficient analysis as validating simulation timescales.

Both address simulation methodology and validation (C30-C34, C105-C108). OpenEval supports the large trajectory count and correspondence with cryo-EM. Peer reviewers accept the methodological approach and pH-independence findings, supporting the merged dataset strategy.

Partial overlap on methodological foundation (C18, C20, C21). OpenEval supports the pH-based approximation and prior methodological work. Peer reviewers accept the overall simulation methodology without specifically addressing the pH approximation rationale.

Both address methodological contribution and broader impact (C122-C123). OpenEval supports the integration approach but notes therapeutic implications are speculative. Peer reviewers strongly affirm the methodological contribution and utility for understanding pLGIC-lipid interactions.

Minimal overlap on C38 regarding forked density shapes. OpenEval supports cryo-EM observations and merging justification. Peer reviewers focus on overall structural quality and simulation agreement without specifically addressing forked densities.

Minimal overlap on C108 regarding pH vs conformational state distinction. OpenEval supports this interpretation as justifying dataset merging. Peer reviewers accept pH-independence findings as part of broader methodological validation.

Minimal overlap on C115 regarding outer leaflet variability. OpenEval uses this to support pH/state distinction. Peer reviewers accept state-dependent differences without specifically addressing leaflet-specific variability patterns.

Minimal overlap on C25 regarding lipid site inventory. OpenEval supports the five sites per subunit finding. Peer reviewers accept inner-leaflet sites without specifically addressing the total count summary.

Minimal overlap on C26-C27 regarding site inventory summary. OpenEval supports the integrated findings. Peer reviewers accept state-dependent sites without specifically addressing the inventory summary claims.

OpenEval evaluates background/introduction claims C1-C7 regarding established knowledge and appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than literature review.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C8-C14 regarding prior structural knowledge and knowledge gaps. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not specifically assess introduction/motivation claims.

OpenEval identifies uncertainty regarding cryo-EM/simulation discrepancy for principal-face site (C77-C78, C118-C120). This inconsistency is acknowledged but not resolved. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not specifically address this discrepancy.

OpenEval evaluates lipid composition limitation (C101-C104) regarding POPC vs E. coli lipids, finding the justification reasonable but noting potential impact on head group interactions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific limitation.
